description: Eight polyphonic VCA channels opened and closed by a beat count taken from a divided clock, each with shaped rise and fall and an envelope output

params.text: Divides the clock into beats, which every channel's start and length are counted in; at 1 a beat is a clock pulse
Zeroes the clock and beat counts, and can return the channels to their enabled snapshot
Enables that channel: unlit is disabled, white is enabled, green is active and yellow is overridden
Sets the beat count on which that channel's VCA opens
Sets how many beats that channel's VCA stays open for; 0 holds it open until something else closes it
Sets how long that channel's VCA takes to open, from instant to 60 seconds
Sets how long that channel's VCA takes to close, from instant to 60 seconds
Curves the opening of that channel's VCA, logarithmic to the left, linear in the middle and exponential to the right
Curves the closing of that channel's VCA, logarithmic to the left, linear in the middle and exponential to the right

inputs.text: The clock the module counts; a trigger or a gate works best, though any signal is counted
A trigger zeroes the clock and beat counts, and can return the channels to their enabled snapshot
A positive signal on channels 1 to 8 enables or disables the matching channel, and on channels 9 to 16 flips its active state whatever its start beat says
The polyphonic signal for that channel, which passes through its VCA to the channel output below

outputs.text: A polyphonic pass-through where channels 1 to 8 carry the clock pulses and channels 9 to 16 carry the beat pulses, each present only while its channel is enabled
A trigger when that channel's VCA closes, whether from its length, an override or being disabled
A 10V signal while that channel is active, following its rise and fall times and shapes
That channel's input after its VCA
A trigger when that channel's VCA opens

notes: nothing opens until a clock is patched into the clock input and a channel is enabled
menu: Immediate Slew Reset closes the slews as fast as it can on a reset, rather than letting them follow their fall settings
Reset to Enabled Snapshot returns every channel to the enabled state it had at the last snapshot, and Save Enabled Snapshot overwrites that snapshot
